Several months ago, with primary elections coming up, New York Mayor Zohran
Mamdani and the city chapter of the Democratic Socialists of America decided
to make them a test of strength. Mamdani endorsed three candidates for
Congress, and both he and NYC-DSA [worked
overtime](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/24/nyregion/mamdani-politics-
influence.html) campaigning and fundraising for them.

The election was Tuesday, and the result was a clean sweep for Mamdani's
candidates. His friend Brad Lander easily defeated incumbent Rep. Dan Goldman
in the 10th district, while Claire Valdez defeated Brooklyn borough president
Antonio Reynoso for an open seat in the 7th district. In a shocking upset,
former Mamdani campaign volunteer Darializa Avila Chevalier defeated Rep.
Adriano Espaillat, a five-term incumbent and the chair of the Congressional
Hispanic Caucus, in the 13th district.

Mamdani and his DSA allies are proving to be something of local kingmakers -
and[ fairly cutthroat ones
too](https://www.cnn.com/2026/06/24/politics/zohran-mamdani-democrat-anger-
primaries). Espaillat endorsed Mamdani for the general election in the mayor's
race, while Nydia Velazquez - the 7th district's retiring incumbent, who
supported Reynoso - endorsed Mamdani for the primary.

For Mamdani, playing nice with establishment Democrats is evidently not as
important as building up his political power base and putting allies into key
positions.
